stem.text: The function r is continuous and \( r(t) > 0 \) for all t. Let \( H(x) = \int_{0}^{x} 2\left(t - 4\right)\left(t - 9\right)r(t)\,dt \) for \( 0 < x < 5 \). Find the value of x in \( 0 < x < 5 \) at which H has a critical point, and determine whether H has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither there. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: At x = 4 only; H has a relative maximum there because H' changes from positive to negative at x = 4.

worked_solution.text: \( H'(x) \) is \( 2\left(x - 4\right)\left(x - 9\right) \) times \( r(x) \), which is positive, so \( H'(x) = 0 \) only where \( 2\left(x - 4\right)\left(x - 9\right) = 0 \), at x = 4 and x = 9.
Only x = 4 lies in \( 0 < x < 5 \); x = 9 is greater than every x in the range.
On the range the factor \( \left(x - 9\right) \) keeps one sign, so H' changes from positive to negative at x = 4, and H has a relative maximum there.

options.label: At x = 4 only; H has neither there because H' stays close to 0 on both sides of x = 4.
options.derivation: the point classified by the size of the derivative nearby rather than by whether its sign changes

options.label: At x = 4 only; H has a relative maximum there because H' changes from positive to negative at x = 4.
At x = 4 and x = 9; H has a relative maximum at x = 4 and a relative minimum at x = 9 because H' changes sign at each.
options.derivation: the zero x = 9 of the derivative kept although it lies outside the stated range

options.label: At x = 4 only; H has a relative minimum there because H' changes from positive to negative at x = 4.
options.derivation: the direction of the sign change read the wrong way round in the classification
